title: Emergency Medicine
description: Emergency Medicine — acute presentations and management.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with ischemic heart disease developed dizziness and confusion following accidental ingestion of a higher dose of atenolol. Blood pressure 70/40 mmH Heart rate 46 /min In addition to holding atenolol and administration of intravenous fluid, which of the following drugs is the most appropriate?

A 23-year-old woman is brought to the Emergency Department after she ingested 15 tablets of paracetamol in a suicidal attempt 6 hours earlier. Activated charcoal is administered by the Emergency doctor. Which of the following is the best next option in management?
Which of the following is the best initial management?

A 55-year-old man presents in the Emergency Department with nausea, pallor and lethargy. He has no past medical history of note. On examination, he has normal vital signs and unremarkable systemic examination (see lab results and report). Sodium 139 (134-146 mol/L) Potassium 6.9 (3.5-5.1 mmol/L) Bicarbonate 14 (21-28 mmol/L.) Blood urea nitrogen 14 (2.8 to 8.9 mmol/L) Creatinine 240 (44-115 mol/L) ECG: Showed tall peaked T waves. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

A 55-year-old man is seen in the Emergency Department complaining of lethargy for the last 2 days. On physical examination, vital signs are stable with unremarkable physical examination. ECG shows no acute changes (see lab results). Sodium 139 (134-146 mmol/L) Potassium 6.6 (3.5-5.1 mmol/L) Bicarbonate 15 (21-28 mmol/L) Blood urea nitrogen 9 (2.8 to 8.9 mmol/L) Creatinine 118 (44-115 mol/L) Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

A 25-year-old woman is brought to the Emergency Department after being rescued from a burning house after 2 hours. She is drowsy, and covered in black soot. On examination, she has 35% burns and nostrils and mouth are filled with soot. After initial resuscitation, her carboxyhemoglobin levels are raised (40%). Blood pressure 90/50 mmg Heart rate 125 /min Respiratory rate 32 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 22-year-old complains of a 2-day history of right sided chest pain and dyspnoea. It started during landing from a long flight. On examination, he is tall, breath sounds are absent on the right side and the percussion note is resonant (see report). CXR: Right pneumothorax. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

A 53-year-old woman known diabetic presented to the Emergency Department with 5-days history of progressive redness and pain on her right thigh. On examination, right thigh showed 15 cm red lesion, which was tender with no ulcer (see report). Temperature 38.3 °C. Ultrasound: Showed inflammatory changes and 10 x 8 cm deep abscess collection. Which of the following is the best management approach?

options.text: Admit to ward and start IV antibiotics
Admit to ICU and start IV antibiotics
Discharge home on oral antibiotics with 1-week follow up
Admit to ward, start IV antibiotics, and surgical consultation

questions.stem: A 45-year-old diabetic woman presented to Emergency Department with fever, flank pain and dysuria. She is allergic to penicillin. Examination shows flank tenderness (see lab result and report). Temperature 39 °C WBC 17 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Urine culture: > 100.000 cfu/ml E.coli. Which of the following is absolutely contraindicated?

A 45-year-old woman presented to Emergency Department with fever, flank pain and dysuria (see lab result and report). WBC 14 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Urine culture: > 100,000 cfu/ml E.coli Which of the following is the best empirical treatment option?

A 48-year-old diabetic woman presented to Emergency Department with dysuria (see lab result and report). WBC 14 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Creatinine 230 44-115 mol/L Urine culture: > 100,000 cfu/ml E.coli Which of the following medications is contraindicated?

A 27-year-old man admitted to the Intensive Care Unit 4 weeks ago with severely infected necrotizing pancreatitis. He underwent several interventions for sepsis control and drainage of collection. He is on mechanical ventilation and inotropes. Which of the following metabolic responses is most expected?

A 38-year-old man who is known to have Crohn's disease, presented to the Emergency Department with a history of 8-12 episodes of diarrhoea per day over the last 5 days. On examinations, he was dehydrated; abdomen was distended with generalised muscle weakness (see report). ECG: Flattened T-waves. Which of the following is the most likely electrolyte abnormality?

A 55-year-old woman known to have chronic duodenal ulcer, presented to the Emergency Department with a history of frequent vomiting for 2 weeks. Examination revealed dehydration , with distended upper abdomen and normal bowel sounds (see report). Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy: Severely narrowed pylorus due to chronic peptic ulcer disease. Which of the following is the most expected?

A 36-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department with a history of right iliac fossa pain for 9 days associated with fever and vomiting. Physical examination revealed tender abdominal mass in the right iliac fossa with sluggish bowel sounds (see report). Temperature 39 °C CT scan: Appendicular abscess, 15 x 18 cm in size, in the right iliac fossa. Which of the following is a characteristic pathophysiology?

A 20-year-old man was brought to the Emergency Department, 20 minutes after a motor vehicle accident. On examination, his extremities were warm, he was conscious, oriented with a clear chest and normal abdomen. Blood pressure 90/40 mmH Heart rate 70 /min Which of the following is the most likely type of shock?

A 21-year-old man was brought to the Emergency Department following a motorbike crash, complaining of difficulty in breathing. On examination, he was conscious, oriented, dyspnoeic with reduced breath sounds and tympanic percussion over the left hemithorax. Blood pressure 90/55 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Chest tube insertion in the left hemithorax

questions.stem: A patient presented with severe diarrhoea. Which of the following are the most expected abnormalities?
A patient presented with severe maxillofacial injury with mandibular fracture dislocation and profuse oral bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to secure the airway?
A patient presented with frequent vomiting due to gastric outlet obstruction Which of the following is the most expected abnormalities?

An 18 year-old woman developed urticaria and wheezing following intravenous injection of contrast for abdominal CT scan. Blood Pressure 90/50 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Temperature 37.2 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate therapy?

A 45-year-old man involved in a motor vehicle accident with an isolated head injury, remains in coma for 5 days after the accident. Which of the following is the most appropriate feeding method in the early stage of management?

A 64-year-old man with emphysema was admitted with hematemesis. On endoscopy, a bleeding duodenal ulcer was diagnosed and controlled but the patient became confused and agitated (see lab results). ABG PCO2 75 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.23 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 42 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy?

A 35-year-old man with a history of open appendectomy 5 years ago presented with abdominal pain, distension, vomiting and constiopation for 3 days. On physical examination, he was dehydrated, abdomen was distended with marked tenderness in the right iliac fossa and exaggerated bowel sounds. He was scheduled for emergency exploratory laparotomy (see report). Plain abdominal X-ray: Distended small bowel, multiple air fluid levels with collapsed colon. Which of the following is contraindicated?

A 37-year-old man with a history of chronic duodenal ulcer, presented to the Emergency Department complaining of frequent postprandial vomiting since last 2 weeks. On physical examination, he was dehydrated with positive succussion splash when shaking the abdomen. which of the following is the most expected acid-base abnormality?

A 67-year-old man, known to have advanced antral carcinoma with liver metastasis, presented to the Emergency Department with a history of frequent vomiting for 10 days. On examination, he was jaundiced and dehydrated (see report). ECG: Flattened T-wave. Which of the following is the most expected finding in urinalysis?

A 25-year-old man brought to the Emergency Department unconscious with massive bleeding from a stab wound in the right thigh. On examination, he was pale with active bleeding from the stab wound (see lab result). Hb 89 130-170 g/L Which of the following is the most important initial step in management?

A 32-year-old man who is known to have ulcerative colitis , presented to the Emergency Department with a history of frequent attacks of watery diarrhoea for 10 days. On examination, he was severely dehydrated with a non-distended, soft abdomen. Which of the following is the most expected acid-base abnormality?

A 27-year-old woman presented to Emergency Room with right lower abdominal pain for 1 day with vomiting. The Emergency Room physician requested CT scan of the abdomen. Which of the following is the most important information to know?

A 28-year-old pregnant woman in her 34 weeks of gestation presented to Emergency Room with heavy vaginal bleeding. Abruptio placentae is suspected (see lab result). Blood pressure 88/42 mmHg Heart rate 129 /min Respiratory rate 26 /min Oxygen saturation 96 % Hb 86 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Which one of the following is the best next approach to save her life?

options.text: Admission to SICU under obstetric service
Transfusion with 2 units of fresh frozen plasma
Rapid response team with coordinated multi-specialty team

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman presents to the Emergency Department with vomiting and generalized abdominal pain. She does not know her medications. She states that her vision has been slightly yellow tinged recently (see image). Blood pressure 90/50 mmHg Heart rate 60 /min Respiratory rate 16 /min Temperature 37° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old drug addict man presents to the Emergency Department with 1-hour history of unconsciousness. On examination, he has pinpoint pupils and a respiratory rate of 8/minute. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 53-year-old woman with history of depression presents to the Emergency Department with history of nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, tinnitus, and shortness of breath 6 hours after consuming 50 tablets of aspirin (see lab result). Plasma salicylate concentration 54 15-30 mg/dL which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
